title: A Navi Mumbai port just moved more containers in a single month than ever before. November 6, 2026.
excerpt: From Gandhi's arrest leading a march across a South African border, to a Telangana village girl now mayor of a Sydney city, to a Navi Mumbai port breaking its own container record a month after setting it, to a Chhattisgarh farmer whose crop switch finally made the numbers work - November 6's four stories are about movements that keep gaining ground.
bodyHtml:
Every story today is about momentum that didn't stop at the first win - a march that kept going after an arrest, a political career built one election at a time, a port record broken again within weeks, and a household budget that finally balanced after one hard decision.

He led over 2,000 miners and laborers across a border - and got arrested for it. Twice

On November 6, 1913, Mohandas Gandhi led roughly 2,221 Indian miners and laborers across the Natal-Transvaal border at Volksrust, South Africa, protesting a discriminatory tax. He was arrested, released on bail, rejoined the march, and was arrested again - a campaign that led directly to the Indian Relief Act of 1914.

She grew up in a Telangana village. In September 2026, she became mayor of an Australian city

Sandhya 'Sandy' Reddy was elected Mayor of Strathfield Council, Sydney, on September 29, 2026. Born in Telangana, she moved to Australia in 1991 and built her political career from councillor to deputy mayor to mayor over five years.

A Navi Mumbai port just moved more containers in a single month than ever before

Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority handled 834,697 TEUs in September 2026 - its highest-ever monthly volume, up 28.63% year-on-year - edging past its own record set just one month earlier in August.

Her family's farming barely covered expenses. She switched crops - and her income finally caught up

Purnima, from Balrampur district, Chhattisgarh, joined a Self-Help Group and became a 'Lakhpati Didi' by switching to organic Jiraphool rice farming - a decision that now covers household expenses and her children's education.

Four stories, one pattern: a march that didn't stop at the first arrest, a career built one election at a time, a record broken again within weeks of the last one, and a household that finally balanced after one hard decision.
